rashi:a1.1: Had two come upon her, one in an atypical manner: first, and afterward this one came upon her in the typical manner, for she was still a virgin and is owed the fine. [People will say:] this one, who had intercourse with a tainted woman, where there is not so much humiliation, gives fifty sela, while had he had intercourse with a wholly untainted virgin he too would give only fifty. But as it is now, with humiliation there is a distinction, for he pays more for the humiliation of an untainted woman than of a tainted one.
rashi:a2.1: Afflicted with boils: he is tainted [i.e., of lesser value], like the woman who had intercourse in an atypical manner.
rashi:a3.1: Because he tormented her: the beginning of the verse is “Then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty silver shekels” (Deuteronomy 22:29), which implies that these fifty silver shekels he gives as the fine for the torment. And since the verse had to write this, it may be inferred that he is liable for other things, such as humiliation and degradation, which are not the fine for the torment, since even without torment there is humiliation and degradation. [Degradation] is the loss: that she is now worth less than at first.
rashi:a6.1: Mishna. It is found that one who utters with his mouth is more severe: for he gives one hundred sela, while one who commits the act of raping a virgin gives only fifty.
rashi:a6.2: The sentence: that they would not enter the Land.
rashi:a6.3: “These [zeh] ten times”: this is written regarding the spies, and it implies that over this [zeh] the sentence was sealed.
rashi:a7.1: Gemara. From where: [is it proven] that one who utters with his mouth is more severe, which implies that he gives them [the hundred sela] on account of the malicious speech alone? Perhaps this malicious speech is more severe because it can bring about her death.
rashi:a8.1: Because he has defamed: on account of the malicious speech alone.
rashi:a9.1: “In the fullness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”: when his se’a is filled with many sins, then “he shall be in straits”: trouble will come upon him.
rashi:a10.1: Over this it was sealed: and not because it combined with the others.
rashi:a12.1: The owner: the Holy One, Blessed be He.
rashi:a13.1: For the evil report of the land that they brought: the verse says that they died [for that].
rashi:a17.1: That his master gives him a gift: food for the fish.
rashi:a17.2: One and a half: for regarding Pharaoh it is written “six hundred chariots” (Exodus 14:7), and regarding Sisera it is written “nine hundred chariots” (Judges 4:3).
tosafot:a1.1: Had two come upon her, one in the typical manner and one in an atypical manner: Rashi explains that one first had intercourse with her in an atypical manner and then another had intercourse with her in the typical manner, for she was still a virgin and is owed the fine; and people will say: this one, who had intercourse with a tainted woman, where there is not so much humiliation, gives fifty sela, while one who had intercourse with an ordinary, wholly untainted virgin also gives only fifty. And in chapter Ben Sorer UMoreh (Sanhedrin 73b), on the statement that one does not pay until the completion of intercourse, Rashi explained that this means until he removes her virginity, which implies that removing the signs of virginity is required for liability to the fine. But it is not so, for it is stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b): if ten men had intercourse with her and she is still a virgin, that is, they came upon her in an atypical manner, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: I say that the first is stoned and all the others are strangled; and Rabbi Zeira said about this that Rabbi concedes with regard to the fine that they all pay. Therefore the Ri explains: people will say, one who had intercourse with a tainted woman pays fifty gold coins, namely the one who had intercourse with her afterward in the typical manner; and one who had intercourse with an untainted woman pays fifty gold coins, namely the one who first had intercourse with her in an atypical manner, since at that time she was untainted. In any case, according to all the explanations one must say that the one who had intercourse in an atypical manner was first, yet the books read “the one who had intercourse in the typical manner” [first]. And according to the Ri’s explanation it is somewhat difficult, for [the Gemara] could have said: had two men come upon her in an atypical manner.
tosafot:a12.1: “Do not read mimmennu but mimmennu”: [some] explain: do not read mimmennu with a soft [nun] but mimmennu with a dagesh. But it is not so, for every mimmennu in the Torah has a dagesh, and there is no difference at all between the one and the other [the same written word means both “than us” and “than him”]. And so we find in the Sifrei on “Nor was his natural force abated [lo nas leḥoh]”: it is not written here [one way], but rather [read it another way] [the printed text gives the same word twice, so the exact contrast is unclear].
tosafot:a16.1: In brief: Tosafot asks how the Jewish people of that generation could have been of such little faith as to think that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would perform miracles for the Egyptians, bringing them out of their land [across the sea after Israel]. Rabbi [the text gives no further name] answers in the name of his father, Rabbi Shmuel: Israel did not cross the width of the sea from one side to the other, for then they would have hurried on toward Eretz Yisrael. Rather they crossed one strip of the sea lengthwise until they turned toward the wilderness on one side, since they could go no other way without crossing the sea, and the Egyptians were on their right and their left. So “just as we are ascending from this side” into the wilderness, “so too the Egyptians are ascending from another side” of the wilderness and will pursue and overtake us, for they thought the Egyptians would not cross in the sea but would come around another way. This also explains the verse (Numbers 33) “And they journeyed from Marah … and encamped by the Red Sea” [Numbers 33:9–10]: had they crossed the width of the sea to its other shore, how did they meet the sea again? Did they turn back? Rather, it shows that they traveled along the length of the sea and came out likewise along it. Tosafot then traces the route: Egypt lies to the south of Eretz Yisrael toward the west, the Nile separates Egypt from Eretz Yisrael, and the sea runs from east to west south of Egypt; they traveled along the northern shore of the sea, went around like half a round threshing floor, and came out on their northern side, south of Edom and east of Egypt; then they traveled some days to Marah and were still near the sea. And when they had to enter Eretz Yisrael they did not need to cross the sea, but went around the lands of Edom and Moab, south of Eretz Yisrael and east of Egypt. Open on Sefaria for the full text.
tosafot:a17.1: One and a half of theirs: regarding Egypt it is written “six hundred chosen chariots” (Exodus 14:7), and regarding Sisera it is written “nine hundred chariots” (Judges 4:3). And although it is also written there, “and all the chariots of Egypt” (Exodus 14:7), the Gemara counts only [the six hundred]: the officers of the land of Egypt depended on the six hundred chariots, and the kings of Sisera depended on the nine hundred iron chariots. And if the army of men in one was greater than in the other, it does not concern [the Gemara].
gershom:a1.1: It is found that one who utters with his mouth is more severe than one who performs an act: for one who says with his mouth that so-and-so is tainted is more severe than one who taints her himself, since this one gives fifty shekels and that one a hundred.
gershom:a2.1: Had two come upon her, one in an atypical manner and one in the typical manner: the first, who did not have intercourse with her in the typical manner, gives nothing, since he did not [take her virginity] [the printed text refers the reader to Tosafot here]. And if this last one, who had intercourse with her, gave fifty as though he had had intercourse with a wholly untainted woman whom no man had ever come upon, people would say: one who has intercourse with a tainted woman [pays fifty, and one who has intercourse with an untainted woman pays fifty]. Rather, certainly for a tainted woman he gives fifty and no more, since she has already been humiliated, and for an untainted woman he gives fifty plus humiliation.
gershom:a3.1: And so we found [with our ancestors]: as it is written, “yet they have tried Me these ten times,” and right after it, “surely they shall not see the land” (Numbers 14:23). For all those ten times that they tried [Him], not trusting in the Holy One, Blessed be He, the decree that they would fall in the wilderness was not decreed upon them, until they spoke malicious speech about the Land.
gershom:a4.1: Because he has defamed: and they fine him one hundred silver shekels.
gershom:a5.1: “In the fullness of his sufficiency”: when the sins are full, as things fill up a measure to its capacity, “he shall be in straits”: [God] exacts punishment from him.
gershom:a6.1: Wood and stones: as it is written, “the cities are great and fortified up to heaven” (Deuteronomy 1:28), and “it is a land that eats up its inhabitants” (Numbers 13:32).
gershom:a7.1: But “than Him”: toward Above, that is, the Owner who created them.
gershom:a8.1: So too the Egyptians are ascending from another side: even though the Holy One, Blessed be He, had promised them, “you shall see them again no more” (Exodus 14:13).
gershom:a9.1: Spew them out onto dry land: once they are dead.
gershom:a10.1: [Two with water:] at Mara and at Rephidim. And it is difficult for me: why does it not count the water in the wilderness of Zin [Numbers 20]?
rashi:b1.1: Do not go out: on Shabbat, to gather.
rashi:b2.1: With the first quail: when the manna began to fall, the quail came down with it, as it is written (Exodus 16:13): “And it came to pass in the evening, that the quail came up … and in the morning there was a layer of dew.” And after a long time they desired more.
rashi:b4.1: In the wilderness of Paran: the episode of the spies.
rashi:b5.2: “What shall He give you, and what more shall He add for you”: [what more can] the Holy One, Blessed be He, [add as] a guard, so that you will not tell malicious speech?
rashi:b6.1: “Who have said: We will make our tongue mighty”: they are like one who says “Who is lord over us?”, for they deny the fundamental [belief in God].
rashi:b8.1: And a confirmed [muḥlat] leper: evidently atzmit, which the Targum renders with the language of ḥalita [confirmation], refers to leprosy.
rashi:b13.1: “Him [oto] I will not suffer”: in this same verse it is written above, “Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret.”
rashi:b13.2: Concerning the arrogant: [some teach] this statement of Rav Ḥisda about them, for in this verse of “him I will not suffer” it is also written “haughty of eye.”
rashi:b14.1: We read nedunenu [“we will judge him”].
rashi:b16.1: “And perverseness in it [vesalef bah]”: one who perverts [his tongue] with it and wishes to remove it, so that it is no longer in him, should break his spirit.
rashi:b17.1: Karetu: the language of karet [being cut off].
rashi:b20.1: Which of them would be taken out: “great” is written of all of them, so all of them are included.
rashi:b21.1: Third speech: this is the speech of the talebearer, who is a third between a person and his fellow, revealing a secret to him.
rashi:b21.2: The one who speaks it: the talebearer himself; for out of the quarrel that falls between the two, they kill each other, and the blood redeemers kill the talebearer, since the killing came about through him.
rashi:b25.1: One who wants death, by his tongue: let him engage in words of folly and obscenity.
rashi:b25.2: One who wants life, by his tongue: let him engage in Torah.
rashi:b26.1: Fire at so-and-so’s home: implying that he is rich, and fire is always to be found in his house for cooking dishes.
rashi:b26.2: It is merely revealing a matter: since he does not say it as malicious speech, but tells those who are looking for fire: go to so-and-so’s house.
rashi:b27.1: That is said in the presence of its master: that the talebearer says it in the presence of the one he is speaking about.
rashi:b27.2: And turned around behind me: to see who might be standing behind me, for I would say it even in the presence of the people concerned; evidently, it is not considered malicious speech. Another version: if the people concerned came and asked, “Why did you say this?”, I never went back on it and said “I did not say it”; rather I admitted it to their faces.
tosafot:b2.1: They desired a desire: Rashi explains “they desired more,” implying that the quail had not stopped coming for them. [The printed text then names] Rashi and Rabbi Yosef Kara: [one] explained that the first quail had stopped, and “the mixed multitude that was among them desired a desire” because they had no quail, and then the second quail came down for them.
tosafot:b9.1: Reish Lakish says: what is the meaning of that which is written, “This shall be the law of the leper [metzora]”? The law of a defamer [motzi shem ra]: we read “Reish Lakish says,” and not “And Reish Lakish says,” since Reish Lakish said nothing above [in this passage].
tosafot:b21.1: Third speech: Rashi explains: the third speech, that of the talebearer who reveals a secret. And I found it written: “third tongue,” because the Holy One, Blessed be He, surrounded it with two walls, one of bone and one of flesh, and it is the third, within them.
gershom:b1.1: In the wilderness of Paran: as it is [described], at the time the spies came.
gershom:b2.1: [“What shall be given to you” etc.: that is, what could I have done for you, for your own good, that I have not done? Why, then, are you deceitful?]
gershom:b3.1: One of bone and one of flesh: teeth and lips.
gershom:b4.1: “If the serpent bites without charming”: that is, the serpent bites in a place where there is no charmer to charm it. And some explain “If the serpent bites without a whisper”: that is, it cannot bite unless it was whispered to from Heaven, commanding it.
gershom:b5.1: “There is no advantage to the master of the tongue”: for what benefit does the master of the malicious tongue have in speaking malicious speech? So [the serpent] has found itself a companion.
gershom:b6.1: “And have cast stones upon me”: this is the stone they placed over the mouth of the pit when they cast Daniel into it.
gershom:b8.1: “And perverseness in it [vesalef bah]”: one who has perverted his tongue with it.
gershom:b9.1: “A broken spirit”: let him humble his mind.
gershom:b10.1: Increases sins corresponding to three transgressions: for of those only “great” is written, and here “great things” is written.
gershom:b11.1: But say two: [corresponding to two transgressions], for “great things” implies only two. [Which of them would you take out? Of all of them “great” is written.]
gershom:b12.1: Third speech: for the one who speaks heard it from one person and told it to another, so that there are three people.
gershom:b13.1: [“They have set their mouth against the heavens”: for one can kill with malicious speech as far as the end of the world.]
gershom:b14.1: From close by: [only] as far as his fist reaches.
gershom:b15.1: [One who wants life, by his tongue: that he engages in Torah.]
gershom:b16.1: Who says, “There is fire at so-and-so’s home”: when people ask, “Where can we get fire?”, and he says, “There is some at so-and-so’s house, where they prepare food all day.”
gershom:b17.1: I never said a thing and then turned around: that is, when I would say something about anyone, I did not need to turn around and look to see that the person concerned was not there; for even if he were there, I would not worry, since I do not lie and do not say it as malicious speech.
